sections.title: Player-facing description
sections.body: A warm warded community of food, repairs, arguments, Firstmoss glow, shoes-off customs, and people trying to keep ordinary life ordinary.

sections.title: Public role
sections.body: Make Hush feel worth protecting before the finale asks the party to protect it.

sections.title: Handout text
sections.body: A real village under corporate designation, protected by ward pillars.

sections.title: GM truth
sections.body: Hush is never the joke. The joke is the system that renamed a real place as a managed endpoint and underfunded its protection.

sections.title: GM handling
sections.body: Introduce with sensory texture, then make one discoverable clue or social choice visible.

sections.title: Mechanics
items: Title: Location Exploration Mechanics
Player Safe: Players can navigate, search, read customs, inspect hazards Hush when it is present in the fiction.
Gm Only: Use the roll only when the player's method, stakes, and consequence are concrete.
No Roll Reveals: Surface read: A real village under corporate designation, protected by ward pillars. Give obvious visible facts freely; roll for meaning, risk, leverage, cost, or a hidden angle.

Rolls: entity-hush-engage-hush entity-hush Engage Hush Engage Hush Instinct Knowledge Finesse Presence Instinct Knowledge, Finesse, Presence 13 Choose the trait from the player's method, not the entity type. A flat read of Hush hides the cost, motive, or useful next step. Critical Success: best possible version of the action; gain Hope and clear 1 Stress. Add an extra benefit that follows from the fiction. Success with Hope: the PC gets what they wanted and gains Hope. Keep the position clean or generous. Success with Fear: the PC gets what they wanted, but the GM gains Fear and introduces a cost, complication, or pressure. Failure with Hope: the PC does not get the full result, but gains Hope and receives a useful thread, clue, or safer next option. Failure with Fear: the PC fails and the GM gains Fear. Make a hard move that follows from the fiction. A flat read of Hush hides the cost...
Fear Spends: Reveal who benefits from the current situation. Make the cost personal without closing off player agency.
Condition Options: No official condition unless a hazard creates Hidden, Restrained, or Vulnerable
Search Loot: Not lootable; offers supplies if trust is earned.

Hush is warm before it is safe: low roofs, clover smoke, hand-repaired doors, and ward posts humming just a little off-key. Hush feels walkable in every direction: canals, porches, co-op warmth, moss farms, quiet gossip, low bridges, laundry, water gates, and neighbors who know the sound of every footstep. The place breaks into usable table spaces: Canal arrival: Low bridges and lantern reflections make the first approach soft and watchful. Porch ring: Homes face shared paths more than private yards. Block2: A village built for working hands, with shoes lined near thresholds and adults quietly tracking the sealed crate. Children watch from behind people they trust; nobody runs, but nobody relaxes until the party proves how they arrived. The ward chimes lag half a beat behind each other. Corporate plaques use the trademarked name, while locals speak around it like an old irritation. Detail Bread, wet clover, hearth smoke, and clean laundry under a mineral edge from the failing wards. Block4: The place changes even if the PCs stand still. Local people, creatures, weather, signage, and ward behavior all keep moving around the scene. Outsider authority can chill the welcome. Bad news from the road spreads faster than the party can control. The Keystone crate makes private fear visible. A child repeats a corporate phrase that makes the room go quiet. A ward chime misses a beat during a tense question. Someone recognizes Tamsin's effects before the party is ready to explain. Let the place be funny through overconfident signage, awkward forms, stubborn local habits, and magic that refuses corporate language.
